title: CSV load rejects files with duplicate headers and silently drops cells from over-long rows (loss becomes permanent on save-back)
existing_state: Two robustness gaps in CsvManager.LoadFromFile: (1) duplicate column names — common in spreadsheet exports, and including the case where any later column is literally named "Host_IP" (the first header is unconditionally discarded and replaced with Host_IP at Services/CsvManager.cs:32-35) — make `dt.Columns.Add(headerName)` (:46) throw DuplicateNameException, surfaced as a raw "Failed to load CSV: A column named 'X' already belongs to this DataTable" dialog (Form1.cs:9239-9242); the file cannot be opened at all. Note headers also collapse via the space->underscore rewrite (:45), so "port 1" and "port_1" collide. (2) Rows with more cells than the header are truncated without any warning (Array.Resize at :61-62); because saving writes the grid back over the same file (Form1.cs:9285-9325), one load-then-save round trip permanently deletes the extra columns' data from the user's file.
recommendation: In LoadFromFile: deduplicate header names deterministically (append _2, _3...) instead of letting DataTable throw, treat a non-first "Host_IP" header the same way, and count truncated rows — return or expose a load summary so Form1 can show "N rows had extra fields that were ignored" before the user saves over the original.
user_benefit: Real-world spreadsheet exports load instead of erroring, and a quiet open/save cycle can no longer permanently strip data out of the operator's hosts file.
